title: Memory card read/write error
shortDescription: Camera cannot access the inserted memory card.
fullDescription:
Sony Alpha cameras display E:61:00 when the body fails to read or write to the installed SD/CFexpress card. The card may be corrupted, dirty, incompatible with the camera's speed class, or formatted on another device.

Counterfeit cards and cards near end-of-life commonly trigger this. Reformatting in-camera usually clears transient cases; persistent errors point to a failing card.

causes.cause: Corrupted file system on the card

fixSteps.title: Power off and reseat card
fixSteps.instruction: Turn the camera off, remove the card, inspect contacts, reinsert firmly.

fixSteps.title: Format in camera
fixSteps.instruction: After backing up, use Menu > Format to re-create the file system.

fixSteps.title: Try a known-good card
fixSteps.instruction: Test with a different genuine card to isolate card vs slot.

whenToCallPro: If a known-good card fails too, the slot itself likely needs service.
videoSearchQuery: Sony Alpha E:61:00 memory card error fix

faq.a: Yes, back up first via a card reader if possible.

title: Lens communication error
shortDescription: The body cannot communicate with the attached lens.
fullDescription:
E:62:00 on Sony Alpha bodies indicates the lens contacts or electronics are not responding. Often caused by dirty contacts, an improperly seated lens, or third-party adapters/lenses with outdated firmware.

Seating issues resolve with a reseat; persistent cases need contact cleaning or firmware updates.

fixSteps.title: Reseat the lens
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the lens, align the white dot, rotate until it clicks.

fixSteps.title: Clean contacts
fixSteps.instruction: Use a dry microfiber to wipe the gold contacts on both lens and body.

fixSteps.title: Update firmware
fixSteps.instruction: Check Sigma/Tamron/Sony support for lens firmware updates.

whenToCallPro: If mount pins look bent or cleaning does not restore communication.

faq.q: Does this happen more with third-party lenses?
faq.a: Yes, Sigma/Tamron MC-11 adapters are common culprits.

title: Power supply / battery communication error
shortDescription: Camera detects an incompatible or faulty battery.
fullDescription:
C:13:01 appears when the Alpha body cannot authenticate the battery, commonly with third-party NP-FZ100/FW50 clones. It can also indicate a genuine battery with failing cells.

Swapping to a genuine, freshly charged battery usually clears the code.

fixSteps.title: Use a genuine Sony battery
fixSteps.instruction: Insert a Sony-branded NP-FZ100 or equivalent and retry.

fixSteps.title: Clean contacts
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe battery and camera terminals with a dry cloth.

fixSteps.title: Update camera firmware
fixSteps.instruction: Some firmware updates expand battery compatibility.

whenToCallPro: If genuine batteries still trigger the code.

faq.a: Not always, but they are the most common cause of C:13 errors.

title: Battery cannot be used
shortDescription: Battery failed authentication or is defective.
fullDescription: Variant of C:13:01 showing a battery the camera refuses outright. Commonly seen after firmware updates that tighten the battery whitelist.

fixSteps.title: Replace with genuine battery
fixSteps.instruction: Only Sony NP-FZ100 (or body-matched) is guaranteed to work after recent firmware.

whenToCallPro: Rarely needed; mostly a battery swap.

faq.a: Sony does not support official firmware downgrade.

title: In-body stabilizer not unlocked
shortDescription: IBIS sensor stuck or failed to center on power-up.
fullDescription:
Sony Alpha bodies display 'Err' when the 5-axis IBIS unit fails its self-test. This can follow drops, power loss during startup, or stuck mechanical lock.

A clean power cycle often releases the sensor; repeated errors indicate IBIS hardware damage.

fixSteps.title: Full power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Remove battery for 60 seconds, reinsert, power on.

fixSteps.title: Update firmware
fixSteps.instruction: Install latest body firmware from Sony support.

whenToCallPro: If sensor is visibly tilted or rattles; IBIS repair requires Sony service.

faq.q: Can I shoot with IBIS off?
faq.a: Sometimes disabling SteadyShot in menu allows shooting until service.

title: Internal temperature too high
shortDescription: Camera is shutting down to protect sensor electronics.
fullDescription:
Long 4K/8K video, hot ambient temperature, or continuous high-fps bursts cause Sony Alpha bodies to hit their thermal limit. A thermometer icon precedes auto-shutdown.

Menu > Auto Power OFF Temp set to 'High' and removing the body from direct sun typically restores recording.

fixSteps.title: Set Auto Power OFF Temp to High
fixSteps.instruction: Menu > Setup > Auto Power OFF Temp > High.

fixSteps.title: Shade the camera
fixSteps.instruction: Remove direct sun; open rear screen away from body.

whenToCallPro: Only if overheating occurs at idle in normal temps — then service.

faq.a: Yes, cages with fans (Tilta, SmallRig) extend record times significantly.

title: Battery depleted / will not hold charge
shortDescription: Battery drops to empty rapidly or will not charge.
fullDescription:
After ~500 cycles NP-FZ100 and older FW50 cells lose capacity. The camera may show full then drop to 0% within minutes.

A calibration cycle (full charge, full drain, full charge) can recover minor cases; otherwise replacement is required.

fixSteps.title: Try a different charger
fixSteps.instruction: Use the original BC-QZ1 or USB-PD charger.

fixSteps.title: Replace battery
fixSteps.instruction: Purchase genuine NP-FZ100 if degraded beyond use.

affectedModels: All Sony Alpha bodies using NP-FZ100 / NP-FW50
whenToCallPro: If camera does not charge any known-good battery, service the charge circuit.
videoSearchQuery: Sony NP-FZ100 battery not charging fix

faq.a: Most users see noticeable drop after 400-600 cycles.

title: SD card lock tab set to LOCK
shortDescription: Physical lock slider on SD card prevents writes.
fullDescription:
Sony bodies refuse to shoot when the SD card's mechanical write-protect tab is in the LOCK position. The slider sometimes slips during insertion.

Eject, slide the tab up toward the contacts, reinsert.

causes.cause: Broken lock tab stuck in LOCK

fixSteps.title: Unlock the card
fixSteps.instruction: Slide the tab on the left edge up toward the contacts.

fixSteps.title: Tape the tab
fixSteps.instruction: If the tab is broken, a small piece of tape can hold it unlocked.

affectedModels: All Sony Alpha models with SD slot
videoSearchQuery: Sony SD card locked write protect fix

faq.a: Worn tabs; replace the card or tape it.

title: Shutter mechanism error
shortDescription: Mechanical shutter failed its cycle check.
fullDescription:
E:50:00 indicates the mechanical shutter did not return to the expected position. Common after the shutter reaches its rated life (~200,000 actuations on pro bodies, less on entry-level).

Switching to electronic shutter may let shooting continue until a shutter replacement is performed.

fixSteps.title: Switch to electronic shutter
fixSteps.instruction: Menu > Shutter Type > Electronic for silent operation as a workaround.

fixSteps.title: Book service
fixSteps.instruction: Shutter replacement is a Sony service center job.

whenToCallPro: Always — shutter replacement is not DIY.

faq.q: Does electronic shutter ever fully replace?
faq.a: For stills mostly yes, but fast motion causes rolling-shutter distortion.

title: Memory card not inserted or not detected
shortDescription: Camera does not see any card in either slot.
fullDescription:
Body reports 'No Card' if the slot is empty or a card is not seated. With dual-slot bodies, the active slot setting must match the inserted card.

Check Rec Media Settings and verify seating.

fixSteps.title: Reseat card
fixSteps.instruction: Push card in fully until it clicks.

fixSteps.title: Check record media setting
fixSteps.instruction: Menu > Rec Media Settings > confirm correct slot.

whenToCallPro: If multiple known-good cards are not detected.

faq.a: No, either slot works if that slot is selected.

title: General internal error
fullDescription: E:91:xx codes indicate internal firmware failures. Often cleared by a firmware update or factory reset; persistent codes indicate mainboard issues.

fixSteps.title: Reinstall firmware
fixSteps.instruction: Download and install the latest firmware from Sony.

whenToCallPro: If reset and firmware reinstall do not clear the code.

faq.a: Yes, but your menu customizations will be lost.

title: External flash fails to communicate
shortDescription: Multi-interface shoe flash not detected or not triggering.
fullDescription: When a Sony flash (HVL-F60RM, F46RM) or third-party (Godox) unit fails to communicate, blinking icons appear and the flash won't fire. Usually caused by dirty shoe contacts, misalignment, or wireless channel mismatch.

fixSteps.title: Clean and reseat flash
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe the MI shoe, slide flash fully forward, lock ring.

fixSteps.title: Match channels
fixSteps.instruction: Set same radio channel and group on commander and remote.

affectedModels: All Sony bodies with MI shoe
whenToCallPro: If MI shoe itself is damaged or pins are bent.
videoSearchQuery: Sony flash not firing MI shoe fix

faq.a: Only via an adapter; modern MI shoe is different.
